summary: Former BC fire lookout overlooking Tochcha Lake, northwest of Vanderhoof; sources give no build, staffing or current-condition history.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.ca calls it a former BC Fire Lookout; no source read says whether the tower still stands.

visit.trail_note: Access is off Tochcha East Road, northwest of Vanderhoof, as described by Firelookout.ca. No hike or road condition is recorded.

evidence.supports: Former BC fire lookout overlooking the shores of Tochcha Lake
evidence.quote: this former BC Fire Lookout overlooks the shores of Tochcha Lake

evidence.supports: Access off Tochcha East Road, northwest of Vanderhoof
evidence.quote: Access is off Tochcha East Road, northwest of Vanderhoof.

evidence.supports: Index files the site under Bulkley - Nechako

evidence.quote: E side of Tochcha Lake, S of Takla Landing

evidence.supports: Name origin: caribou horns once found on the mountain
evidence.quote: The name is a reference to the number of cariboo horns which were once to be found here

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.ca gives 1,535 m (5,040 ft); the web index gives 1,528 m, seven metres lower. Both are reported in the story; the seven-metre gap is not resolved.

sources.title: Deescius
sources.publisher: Canada Lookouts (web index of Canadian lookouts)

notes_for_editor: Sources give no build date, builder, staffing, fire or current-site information. The BC Geographical Names record names the mountain, and its position is about 100 m from the index coordinates (computed from the degrees-minutes-seconds value and the index's decimal coordinates), but no source says the lookout stands on that mountain, so the story says only that the two may refer to the same high ground. The Firelookout.ca page is script-loaded; only its description text was readable. Search turned up no further lookout history; reads were limited to the three sources cited above.
